title: Kth Largest Element in a Stream
description:
# Kth Largest Element in a Stream

Implement `KthLargest` to retain the initial array values and all later insertions, including duplicates:

* `KthLargest(int k, int[] nums)` initializes a fixed positive rank `k` and the initial values `nums`.
* `int add(int val)` inserts `val` and returns the kth largest value after insertion.

Rank values from largest to smallest, counting duplicate occurrences separately. In `[10,9,9,8]`, the third largest is `9`. Every `add` call guarantees at least `k` values after insertion.

In operation examples, the first array lists operations and the second lists their argument lists, paired by index and executed left to right. The first operation constructs the object; later operations use that same object. Outputs align by index too: constructors and void methods produce `null`; an empty argument list `[]` means no arguments.

## Example

Input: `["KthLargest","add","add","add","add","add"]` with `[[3,[4,5,8,2]],[3],[5],[10],[9],[4]]`

Output: `[null,4,5,5,8,8]`

## Constraints

* `k >= 1` and remains fixed after initialization.
* Input values are integers and may be negative, zero, or repeated.
* At least `k` values are available after every `add` call.
initialCode: class KthLargest { public KthLargest(int k, int[] nums) {} public int add(int val) { return 0; } }

solutions.name: Min Heap of Size k
solutions.timeComplexity: O(n log k) init, O(log k) add
solutions.description:
## Approach

Maintain a min heap containing only the k largest values seen so far. The constructor feeds every initial value through the same insertion logic. Each `add` pushes the new value, then removes the heap minimum when the heap grows past k.

## Key Insight

If the heap stores exactly the k largest candidates, the smallest item in that heap is the kth largest item in the full stream. Values smaller than the heap root cannot affect future kth-largest answers unless k changes, and k is fixed.

## Complexity Analysis

Initialization costs `O(n log k)`. Each `add` costs `O(log k)`, and the heap stores `O(k)` values.

solutions.name: Sorted ArrayList with Binary Search Insert
solutions.timeComplexity: O(n log n) init, O(n) add
solutions.description:
## Approach

Keep all stream values in ascending order inside an `ArrayList`. Use binary search to find the insertion index for each new value, insert it, and read the kth largest value at index `size - k`.

## Key Insight

The binary search finds the position quickly, but inserting into the middle of an array-backed list shifts later elements. This route is simple and exact, and it makes duplicate handling visible.

## Complexity Analysis

Initialization costs `O(n^2)` in the worst case with repeated inserts, or `O(n log n)` if built by sorting. Each `add` costs `O(n)` because of shifting. Space is `O(n)`.

solutions.name: TreeMap Multiset
solutions.description:
## Approach

Store value frequencies in a `TreeMap`. After adding the new value, scan keys from largest to smallest and subtract counts until the kth element position is reached.

## Key Insight

A `TreeMap` represents a sorted multiset without storing every duplicate separately. It is useful when many stream values repeat, and it shows why duplicates must count toward the kth position.

## Complexity Analysis

Insertion costs `O(log u)`, where `u` is the number of distinct values. The descending scan costs `O(u)` per `add` in the worst case. Space is `O(u)`.

solutions.name: Quickselect on Demand Baseline
solutions.timeComplexity: O(n) average add, O(n^2) worst-case add
solutions.description:
## Approach

Append every stream value to a list. For each `add`, copy the list into an array and run quickselect for index `size - k` in ascending order. That selected value is the kth largest value.

## Key Insight

Kth largest is the same as the `(n - k)`th item in sorted ascending order. Quickselect teaches the selection view of the problem without maintaining a heap across calls.

## Complexity Analysis

Each `add` uses `O(n)` average time for quickselect and `O(n^2)` worst-case time with unlucky pivots. The stored stream and working copy use `O(n)` space.
